tool.name: HLA typing
tool.description: HLA class I and II alleles from exome reads (T1K), pharmacogenomic HLA alleles and disease associations
tool.command: ln -s '$bam' input.bam && ln -s '${bam.metadata.bam_index}' input.bam.bai && python3 '$__tool_directory__/wes_hla.py' --bam input.bam #if $hla_dat: --hla-dat '$hla_dat' #end if --sample '$bam.element_identifier' --threads \${GALAXY_SLOTS:-4} --min-quality $min_quality --tsv '$types' --json '$summary' --pharmcat '$outside_calls'

param.name: bam
param.label: Aligned reads (BAM)
param.help: Duplicate-marked reads of the sample on GRCh38 (chromosome 6 named 6 or chr6), with the unmapped reads kept, as the FASTQ workflow writes them.

param.name: hla_dat
param.label: HLA allele database (IPD-IMGT/HLA hla.dat)
param.help: hla.dat of an IPD-IMGT/HLA release (https://ftp.ebi.ac.uk/pub/databases/ipd/imgt/hla/hla.dat; the install script's data stage downloads it). T1K's allele reference is built from it in each job (about 15 s). Without it nothing is typed and the outputs say so.

param.name: min_quality
param.label: Lowest T1K quality of a confident call
param.help: T1K's allele quality ranges from 0 to 60. Below it, or when the candidate alleles differ at two fields, the call is marked low confidence and is not passed to PharmCAT.

tool.help:
**What it does**
Types the HLA genes of one exome with T1K 1.0.10 (Song, Bai, Li et al., Genome Research 2023; MIT licence) against the IPD-IMGT/HLA database (Barker et al., Nucleic Acids Res 2023; CC BY-ND 4.0). T1K takes the reads aligned to the HLA genes and the unmapped reads from the BAM, aligns them to every allele, and picks the two alleles per gene that explain the reads best.
**Outputs**
* *HLA types*: for HLA-A, -B, -C, -DRB1, -DRB3/4/5, -DQA1, -DQB1, -DPA1 and -DPB1 the two alleles at two-field (protein) resolution, T1K's quality (0-60), the other equally good candidates and a confidence (high / low / none). A second table lists the pharmacogenomic alleles of CPIC guidelines (HLA-B*57:01 abacavir; HLA-B*15:02 carbamazepine, oxcarbazepine, phenytoin; HLA-A*31:01 carbamazepine; HLA-B*58:01 allopurinol) and the best-known disease associations (HLA-B*27, HLA-B*51, HLA-DQB1*06:02, the celiac-disease DQ2/DQ8 heterodimers). * *summary* (JSON) for the clinical report, with the KIR ligand group of each HLA-A, -B and -C allele, read from its exon 2 (HLA-C residue 80: Asn = C1, Lys = C2; HLA-A/B residues 82-83 Leu-Arg = Bw4, with residue 80 Ile or Thr; HLA-B Arg-Gly = Bw6; HLA-B*46/B*73 Val76 Asn80 = C1), for the KIR tool (wes_kir). * *PharmCAT outside calls*: the HLA-A and HLA-B diplotypes (confident calls only) for the PharmCAT tool, which then gives the CPIC, DPWG and FDA recommendations for these drugs.
**Accuracy** (README section 7): two-field alleles against published types of six GIAB exomes, and Mendelian consistency in three trios.
**Limits**: exome capture covers the exons that define two-field alleles (exons 2-3 of class I, exon 2 of class II); three- and four-field alleles, null alleles from intronic or promoter changes and new alleles are not resolved. A gene with one allele found is homozygous or a missed allele. HLA associations are risk factors, not diagnoses; drug decisions on HLA-B*57:01 or HLA-B*15:02 are usually confirmed with a clinical HLA test.
